key_idea: Strengthen the square function estimate to a multiscale inequality controlled by constants S(r,R), and use Lorentz rescaling to get a submultiplicative recursion (Lemma 9), so that a Kakeya-type L^2 estimate (large r) and parabolic restriction at scale K (small R) can be bootstrapped by induction on scales.
reason: The reformulation into the multiscale quantity S(r,R), together with the rescaling recursion, is a striking and reusable framework that makes the epsilon-loss induction close cleanly. Still, the visible argument carries substantial bookkeeping: weights, local orthogonality, the reduction to Gamma_{1/K} with partitions of unity, and a two-case induction. That puts it at a clearly good level but below a book proof.
recognized: Guth–Wang–Zhang, 'A sharp square function estimate for the cone in R^3' (Annals 2020)
